pos.personaBrief: Liverpool 2021/22 showed 'calmness in possession' and kept the ball with rare finesse, but their danger came from the high press and counter-press where 'the Reds race forward at remarkable speeds'; possession was a tool, not the goal.

pro.personaBrief: Build-up varied between a diamond, 2-5-3 and 3+1 with Fabinho screening, but Alisson 'can go long when pressed', and the counter-press is 'an attacking tool to win the ball back and score quickly'.

est.personaBrief: A fixed 4-3-3 with rehearsed but fluctuating attacking shapes (2-1-4-3, 3-1-6, 2-3-5): wingers narrow into half-spaces, Alexander-Arnold inverts, full-backs and outside midfielders rotate in and out of wide areas.

lar.personaBrief: Width came from the full-backs (Robertson overlapping to cross, in-swinging deliveries) while the wide forwards narrowed into the half-spaces; the flank was used, but not via touchline wingers.

blo.personaBrief: High line pushed to halfway (140 offsides won), league leaders in attacking-third pressures, front three pressing the centre-backs and an immediate counter-press near the ball.

mar.personaBrief: A block of seven closing the centre in zones, with the front three man-marking tightly while covering passing lanes; reads as a zonal block with man-oriented pressing jumps, no dedicated star-markers.

pla.personaBrief: The only PL side to use the same 4-3-3 in all 38 matches, a 'distinctive brand' that stays constant, with Klopp influencing games through second-half substitutions rather than plan changes.

res.personaBrief: A trophy-hunting side (two cups, title and CL final runs) whose identity is loud, intense attacking football; Klopp's 'heavy metal' label and pride in 'how hard they fought' value emotion, but winning is the aim.

sis.personaBrief: A drilled collective where the front three defend five or six players and rotations kept results steady, while forwards like Salah and Díaz were still backed to take on their man.

jog.personaBrief: Intensity was non-negotiable (high press, racing transitions), and Klopp praised Díaz's 'speed, the skillset and the character'; technique mattered but within an athletic, high-running team.

bas.personaBrief: An experienced core with prime-age signings (Konaté, Díaz at 25), but Klopp celebrated that 'Academy, first team, all chipped in' in the cups and Alexander-Arnold was a key academy product.

lid.personaBrief: Klopp widened the players' committee via a dressing-room vote and spoke of pride in 'my boys'; a harmony-first leader who still holds the final word and collective standards.
